I’m glad you liked it because for me it was a bore. As a recreational drug user he does a good job somewhat of expressing the different reactions. 

But the whole thing with the kid and the mob mentality was where he lost me, felt childish. 

I guess the point was to show their regression into evolutionary roles, but I felt it was poorly done. 

As with all his films he has an aesthetic that is very seductive, and he clearly knows his stuff. 

It felt like a lab rat experiment but on people. Which I can appreciate but at some point I just can’t go with it.

Whether it’s because the characters are written so stupidly with no real personality or nuance, or it’s the fact that it is a very mean film that feels like forced schadenfreude. 

He always goes too far, which I can respect it artistically. But he is also very pretentious and cruel with his stories. He is a lover of misery like Lars von Trier, and personally I find it cheap and lacking of substance. No matter how aesthetic their films are they are just miserable and I prefer not to be that ha. 

I get the whole experience of emotion and stuff but it’s just not for me. 

Humans are much better than these films would lead you to believe.

I think the difference between Climax and his previous films is that it's less explicit on all fronts. Climax is my favourite from him, Irreversible is second. It has similar tone to Climax, conveys the anxiety and brutality well but it has 2 very violent scenes. I'm indifferent to the rest of his work, Enter the Void has the hallucinatory quality and neon aesthetic of Climax but it goes on for too long for me and I didn't really care for the framing of the narrative. That being said it has some great sequences. I Stand Alone is pretty nasty from what I remember. Love has plenty of explicit sex, I thought the film itself was all over the place. Vortex is his most subdued film, it's like Amour by Haneke but it uses split screen, he already used split screen in Lux Æterna which seemed like a valid attempt to trigger some epileptic seizure.

>I get the impression he has considered and carefully selected everything on screen. I would love to see the script, to see if every scream was even written out and planned.

Noe works by writing treatments/outlines and then letting people improvise, sometimes that shows quite heavily.

>I think that when you do something out of chaos, it’s fresher. When you over-script something, if you struggle over something or you over-prepare something, it loses its freshness. Movies are about energy, they’re not about scripts. You can start with the energy on the set.  


If you like more Noe you should check out Angst, Dario Argento, Zulawski (there is a tape of Possession in the beginning of Climax, during the interview scene, Zulawski captures madness well. Suspiria is there too) and Philippe Grandrieux.

I consider myself an "interested observer" of Noe's work instead of a fan; I'd quantify the feeling as somewhere above rubbernecking a car crash on the highway. I've seen a few of his films over the years but have found that he often lends himself to extremism without the corresponding emotional heft or intellectual impact that would make the experience worthwhile. It's like he serves up a dish that is excessively spicy but doesn't ever make you feel full.

That said, I watched his most recent release, Vortex, and found that he is certainly innovating new ways to punish his audience in the absence of sex and violence. It is one of his better works that I've seen, although not one that I ever plan to watch again. I thought that Climax was terrible, over-the-top, unfocused, and edgelord-y. It's interesting that you found it to be carefully controlled chaos when a quick look at the pre-production shows that it was actually heavily improvised. 

I think he has a really profound, provoking and impactful movie in him somewhere; if anything I could see him being the perfect director to lead a film about the ongoing conflict between Israel and Palestine (and let's be honest, there will eventually be one). Overall, however, I think his aim is primarily to make the viewer uncomfortable by whatever means available; in my experience with his filmography, that impulse is more often than not unrewarding.

I’m on the same boat. I admire Noé’s films (and Von Trier’s and Haneke’s), there is plenty to analyze and debate about them, but I would never be able to enjoy them in a deep personal level because they are too cruel and focus too much on the text and the moral. There are other filmmakers that are also extremely formalistic (think about Hitchcock, De Palma…) but still retain some playfulness that connects to some positive aspects of the human experience. Not with Noé and the others, there is just misery behind the form.

I really dig _Climax_ and found _Irreversible_ so revolting I almost threw up. This year I watched _Vortex_ which is a very different kind of film but I think you won't regret watching it: it's poignant, crisp, and masterfully executed.

How are his films pretentious? As in, how is he, as an artist, exuding the pretension that he is doing something as a phony? Sure, he has his inspirations in Haneke and Von Trier, but Noe is still breaking new grounds as an artist. He is doing things no one else is doing as an artist. That is, by definition, the lack of pretension. He isnt pretending to do what others do, he is doing exactly what he does, and breaking new territory in art as he does.

I understand not enjoying his films because they are so dark and miserable. But to call Noe pretentious is an incredible disservice to his artistry.

I love Climax, a lot. I love dancing as a tool in film and Climax does some of the best "dancing as storytelling/character building" of any film Ive ever seen.

It gives me a similar feeling to watching Aguirre The Wrath of God. Just humans being boiled down to their basal components in the face of horror. Incredibly disturbing.

As in I think he’s pretentious because he isn’t as smart as he thinks I don’t like how dumbed down his characters are. They feel like vapid shells that serve to push his message, which I think he fails at. His characters are incredibly bare bones and I find it lazy how often he reaches for trauma/violence/sex to try and sell his art.So that’s why I think he’s pretentious.

I just watched possession recently.  That subway scene makes me laugh maniacally and I get a frissant feeling when I watch it. I really can't tell you what it is about that scene that makes feel so much, it's an intangible gnosis kind of feeling.

Im sorry but where in Clinax did you get the impression of "I'm smarter than everyone!! This is a highly intellectual film!!" No, its clearly an emotional story. And to say that he "reaches for violence/trauma/sex" to "sell" his art? 

Come on now. Think a little. He very clearly uses those as central themes of his art. They arent shock factor to sell more. You couldnt remove the violence from Climax, it would be a different film. It is central to the art. It isnt a sales gimmick. Like obviously these themes are very artistically significant to him.

You're really the only one coming off as pretentious here. You don't connect with his art so automatically he's not smart, he can't write, and his characters are shit, and he only makes trauma porn.

The whole film is a lab rat experiment, he is trying to show the effects of the drug on different individuals and different situations. 

It is an interesting idea but he fails at it because of his misanthropic world view, his pretentiousness of looking down on the simple minded characters he has created and the need for excessive trauma/transgressive porn. 

An example of a film that does a better job is A Clockwork Orange. In every way Noe fails were as a Kubrick succeeds. 

The film is empty and annoying, and I have no desire to ever see it again. That is a failure in my book. No matter how artistic or aesthetic it may be.

That's fair. I understand not being able to get past his viewpoint of humanity.

My whole point though is that is his message all the way through. If you disagree with his message, then you disagree with him as a person which is perfectly valid. But to me, calling him pretentious accuses the craft of his art and his level of auteurship, which I think isn't really up for much debate.

And I find it silly that you think his artistic vision is beyond critique. 

It isn’t just him i dislike, it’s also his art. 

You are trying to reduce my opinion into a way that bends to your reality. 

Also that last sentence doesn’t mean anything.

I love all of his films, they depict things in such a real way climax and enter the void feel like a drug trip where as love depicts heartbreak like nothing I’ve ever seen. It’s like cinema version of artaud’s theater of cruelty.

I am saying he is a technically proficient director that displays a lot of style and unique attributes. I am saying he is a true artist, whereas calling him pretentious denies him the state of being a true artist. 

I never said you have to agree with or appreciate his vision. Your opinion is your own. I am stating that it is a *fact* that he is indeed an artist, and calling him pretentious revokes that title from him. He is not pretending to be an artist, he just is.

After some reflection, my whole rant is because I really really hate the criticism of "pretentious" because it really just means nothing. Call it hateful, call it misanthropic, call it mysoginist or really anything else. At least those are real, actionable, specific criticism. Whereas pretentious has come to mean nothing aside from "I want to put this art down." It isnt actionable and it doesnt mean anything.

The worst case (which I don't think you're doing) is when people who don't even attempt to engage with a film and then denounce it. Think a Marvel fan watching the new A24 film and getting bored "This is just boring and pretentious". Kind of thing. 

But it's still bad when it comes into to ttue film criticism. It just seems so lazy and such a shortcut to finding out why you dislike something. Like I said, its purely inactionable critique. I also think its invalid in the sense of, to be pretentious is to pretend to be something you are not. The film maker is literally the film maker, and the critic is literally not. A critic calling a film pretentious is pretty oxymoronic to me.

Also, the idea that pretension is bad is somewhat laughable to me. If Alfred Hitchcock didn't have the pretension that he could direct actors better in a more naturalistic way, then film would be a different landscape. If Kubrick didn't have the pretension that he could effectively adapt novels in an entirely unique and new way, we wouldn't have so many great films. Pretense is the foundation for innovation.

Im all for you hating Gaspar Noe and hating his art. Thats your right as a human. But please come up with better criticisms than pretentious, because that word hurts the entire art community.

I love the mid credits sequence in Climax. The dance scene before it is so intense and hypnotizing, and then inexplicably 45 minutes into the film, credits start rolling. I remember feeling stunned in the theater watching it, both baffled by the purpose of it and also arrested by it.  Now I interpret that scene as the ending of Side A, imagining the movie’s narrative to be inspired by a record with 2 sides,  but I’ll never forget watching it for the first time and experiencing how jarring and exciting that scene was.

Not a big fan of Noe’s other films, but Climax checks all the right boxes for me.

I like Climax quite a bit, and it's an absolute triumph of experimental filmmaking, but it is something of a defanged Enter the Void. Enter the Void takes the character drama that's distributed among all of the (quite thin) improvised characters in Climax, smashes it together in one protagonist, cranks it up to 11, and explores it with a totally maximalist presentation that's arguably Noé's most daring whole.

Classic ‘I don’t like movie = pretentious’ type of argument

- Don’t claim a director is trying to be smarter than they are with regard to a film if you clearly haven’t analyzed it. More depth can be derived from Climax than ‘look what drugs do’ and ‘people are bad’ (I’d argue Climax serves more as an exploration on Noe’s approach to art). To act like an authority on a film’s meaning while clearly not putting much thought into the film makes you pretentious if anything.

- It’s fair to not like Noe’s approach to characters. I think he gives characters more depth than you suggest, but in general his characters serve more to explore his points than be deeply written characters. I don’t see how this is pretentious or inherently bad. Seems just like an approach to utilizing characters you don’t agree with. Just because something deviates from your preference doesn’t make it pretentious.

- Claiming Noe just uses violence/trauma/sex to sell his movies is ridiculous. To suggest these ideas don’t make up genuine major ideas of interest within his work is completely bad faith.

- I guess if you dislike the misanthropic worldview that’s fair. Honestly there’s a decent amount of characters in Climax that aren’t that bad, but in general the film grants a fairly nasty view of humanity. At the very least, he’s trying to highlight humanities worst aspects. I find it interesting, and you are free not to. I don’t see how any of this is pretentious though. Oh right, you don’t agree with the point of view Noe’s presenting. If you personally don’t agree with something, then it must be pretentious (seems to be the logic you’re going with).

- “looking down on simple minded characters he created.” I guess any film with characters that are meant to be disliked is pretentious.

- Everything you said about Climax can easily be said of A Clockwork Orange. Literally everything. With the exception of Alex, characters in A Clockwork Orange aren’t that in-depth. One might say they just exist to push the director’s message. This is true of most of Kubrick’s films. Characterization takes a backseat for him in exchange for other cinematic elements. This is just like Noe, but fine I guess because he’s Kubrick. The same applies to your accusation of misanthropy. Humanity is portrayed horribly in A Clockwork Orange.  Why go on about Noe having a pessimistic worldview you fundamentally disagree with and then bring up a film that, if anything, portrays a bleaker vision of humanity than Climax. By any metric you’ve laid out A Clockwork Orange is pretentious, but according to you it’s actually much better than Climax for some reason. 

If you don’t like Climax, don’t like it. A lot of what you talked about are valid reasons for disliking the film. That doesn’t change how it’s silly to call a film pretentious for clearly no reason other than you not caring for it though.

> there is a tape of Possession in the beginning of Climax

The whole list of books/tapes in the beggining of Climax is quite interesting, haha.

> but still retain some playfulness that connects to some positive aspects of the human experience. Not with Noé and the others, there is just misery behind the form

I mean, to some people life is really miserable most of the time. I know that it is art and it doesn't have to be miserable all the time but sometimes misery and pain are very prevalent in one's life and being able to connect to art that explores this theme feels good.

I loved that film. It lures you with a pure candy opening and candid and real moments when the drug starts to kick in.. then you get the whip. It's delightful. 

It's interesting to see the opinions of people who disliked it being developed here. I see how it could piss someone of if there was noting for you to appreciate in there, it would mean you just get the pain. Then anything potentially good becomes pretentious garbage instead of just not for you.

Noé is a brilliant filmmaker. However we must venture into his filmography with caution and onow it leaves scars. He crushes any glimpse of hope that could reside in our soul. Enter the void is a fairly easy watch. Not a shocking as irreversible. But still leaves a long lasting depressive taste. Irreversible is his best. Very traumatic.

> An example of a film that does a better job is A Clockwork Orange.

I honestly don't see how Orange and Climax are remotely comparable. Why do you think that?

Thank you!!! You said it much better than I could have. Especially your points about A Clockwork Orange. To me, that film is maybe the film with the most pessimistic view of humanity Ive ever seen. Climax sheds light on some of the bright sides of the human spirit even in the darkness. But there is virtually no morality or "goodness" in all of A Clockwork Orange. Not that that specifically makes one film better than the other, just that I can't imagine criticism Climax for being to pessimistic with shallow characters and then offer A Clockwork Orange as the beacon for finding the goodness in humanity.

Loved Climax along with most of Noe's other films.  If you enjoyed the way he captured the drug trip aspect of Climax, then check out Enter the Void, which is basically that same thing, to an even higher degree.  Not my favorite on the whole, but the first act of Enter the Void is gold.

I'd also strongly recommend Irreversible if you think you can handle it.  Noe isn't just throwing shocking content at the audience for shock purposes, as some other  "hard to watch" arthouse films do.  Every part of Irreversible fits together to create a really unique film experience.  Watching it is a real journey.  But it's not for everyone.

Listen, Noe was only made to make one film. Only one. That film was Irreversible. 

Irreversible is the culmination of Noe's abilities. That film stands out among all of transgressional, or extreme, cinema. He manages to shock you, make you so enraged with such a seething and loathsome hatred that you want to personally take on all of the evil in the world. The message that underlies the whole film is what is so important about it. Noe writes a story where he is able to have all the extremist fun he desires; where he can play out all the wild ideas he has; give us an emotional tie to all the characters; and in the end sledgehammer us with a harsh reality that none of us would willing face unless this film existed.

He will never top this. Ever. This is his swan song. Whether he wants it to be or not this was the one great film that he had in him. Since this he has resigned himself to debase his style by obsessing with vapid sensationalism and shocking gimmicks. 

I am harsh towards him because he is a director, who despite all of this, I greatly admire. He continually pushes the edge and explores territory that 'They' deign unworthy. I am not callous towards Noe, I just want to see him realize his potential. He is better than the work he produces. There are moments in other films where we get glimpses of his genius, but then he will cut to some tasteless and undignified affair and it overshadows the whole shine. 

Regardless, I am still a fan of Noe. Visually his films are never boring. Actually, boring and Noe don't fit together in the same sentence. Frustrating is much more apt here. Noe is frustrating.

This movie ruined my day when I first saw it 🤣 marker of quality for sure. As a drug movie, what really stood out to me was that chaotic 'group' feeling. Of so many people lost in the sauce and in their own vibe and everything clashing. All the while merged with the choreography...honestly, maybe his most concise and affecting film. The consequences for the kid...holy fuck. Nightmare fuel.
